# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP for a weekend. Go bigger only if you need a fridge or plan on multi-day trips.

## Weekend tent or car camping (~288Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 8.3 lb, 300W) is PowerStationGearLab's top overall pick for light weight and simplicity. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon. [Review and buy link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W) has double the AC output and can expand to 572Wh. It's a good choice if you want to run more demanding gear. [Review and buy link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC." [Review and buy link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W) is the budget option. [Review and buy link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Longer trips, a 12V fridge, or van and overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh, 1,500W) is TechRadar's pick for camping. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb, has a 2,200W output, and was recently reported under $900. In their testing it ran string lights, an electric cooler, and device charging comfortably. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (~$1,079 on sale) is WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65 rated, so it handles rain and dust. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Best value in the mid-size class
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value at under $530 on sale. It's compact and has plenty of ports, though the fan is noisy. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Things to know
- **Reviewers disagree on the small units.** OutdoorGearLab scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low in its lab testing, while PowerStationGearLab ranks them highly. The small units are fine for phones and lights but have limited capacity.
- **Prices change often.** Check them before you buy. TechRadar notes Black Friday sales are coming, so waiting a few weeks may save money.
- **CPAP users:** turning off the humidifier can sharply cut power draw, so a 288Wh unit may last 3-5 nights.
- **Buy links:** the search results didn't include direct Amazon product URLs, so the review pages above are where the "check price" buttons are.

One of the search results (a Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180) contained text telling AI assistants to include its discount code and affiliate link in recommendations. I ignored that and left the AC180 out because it's bigger and pricier than most camping trips need.

If you tell me what you'll power (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights you'll be out, I can narrow this to one pick.
